overall: Atlanta hit a running max of 89.6°F around 12:50 ET but has since sharply reversed, with current temperature falling to 84.2°F at a steep -5.4°F/hr cooling velocity. The combination of a high dewpoint (73.4°F) and 15 mph winds strongly suggests afternoon convective activity — likely storm outflow or cloud shading — has disrupted the typical peak heating window, making the 89.6°F reading very likely the day's ceiling.
forecast_obs_notes: GFS, ECMWF, and HRRR are tightly clustered at 89.9–90.3°F, slightly above the observed running max, while NBM's more conservative 87.5°F was actually closer to what unfolded — the observed high has already exceeded NBM but fell just short of the three-model consensus. The even ensemble's 90–91°F (Tier 1, high confidence) had the strongest signal, but the odd ensemble's 87–88°F (Tier 4, low credibility) is now moot given that observations have overtaken its range.
max_temp_prediction: With temperatures plummeting at -5.4°F/hr from an already-plateaued peak, and peak solar heating hours (3–4 PM ET) unlikely to overcome the active cooling regime, the daily high is almost certainly already set at 89.6°F. The steep drop is consistent with convective interference rather than a gradual afternoon transition, making a meaningful rebound to the 90–91°F model consensus implausible. Confidence is high (80–85%) that TMAX will finalize at 89.6°F, with a small tail risk to ~90.0°F if the cooling disruption clears briefly.
